en.title: MW4 DMZ Players Divided Over 'Possum' Trait's Game-Breaking Potential
en.summary: A new operator trait in Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode is igniting fierce debate among players. The 'Possum' ability, granting a free revive, is seen by some as a lifeline and by others as a frustrating imbalance.
en.body:
Modern Warfare 4's highly anticipated DMZ mode is officially live, but players are already locked in intense discussions over a controversial new operator trait. Dubbed 'Possum,' this ability, found at the top of the Warfighter operator tree, allows a player to come back to life once per match with no time limit, even after being fully eliminated. This single-use resurrection mechanic is proving to be a significant point of contention, fracturing the community between those who see it as a welcome safety net and those who believe it unfairly disrupts gameplay.

For many, especially solo players or those struggling with the steep learning curve of DMZ, the Possum trait offers a much-needed reprieve. It can mean the difference between losing all your hard-earned gear and getting a second chance to extract. The ability to avoid hefty operator rescue fees after a botched mission is also a significant draw. However, the implications for squad-based combat are where the real friction lies. Opponents who have just eliminated a player are understandably frustrated to see that same operator reappear moments later, potentially turning the tide of a firefight or allowing a downed squad to regroup with minimal penalty, aside from lost inventory.

## The Possum Predicament

The core of the debate centers on the 'one free life' mechanic and its lack of a temporal restriction. Unlike many revival mechanics in gaming that require prompt action or have cooldowns, the Possum trait allows for an indefinite delay before the revival occurs. This means a player could theoretically disengage from combat, wait out a tense situation, and then respawn ready to re-engage or support their team. This flexibility, while beneficial for survival, is seen by many as an exploit that undermines the high-stakes nature of DMZ. The sheer unpredictability of an enemy disappearing and then suddenly reappearing alive, especially in high-traffic POIs, adds a layer of chaos that some players find unfair.

## Community Divided

Reddit and various social media platforms are alight with arguments about the Possum trait. Detractors point to scenarios where a seemingly defeated squad can leverage this mechanic to overwhelm opponents through sheer attrition. The feeling of having a kill 'stolen' or rendered meaningless by an instant revive is a common complaint. Supporters, conversely, argue that it makes the mode more accessible and forgiving, particularly for newer players or those attempting challenging objectives alone. They emphasize that while gear is lost, the opportunity to recover valuable items or complete an objective is preserved, contributing to a more dynamic and less punishing experience. It's clear that this specific trait, designed to offer a second chance, has instead created a significant rift in how players approach and perceive fairness within the DMZ.

## What's Next

While **Activision** has not yet commented on the community's feedback regarding the Possum trait, it's possible that future updates could address the balance concerns. Players will be closely watching for any patches or adjustments to operator abilities that might alter the current meta in **Modern Warfare 4**'s DMZ.

content_raw: Modern Warfare 4 ‘s DMZ mode is finally out after its 2022 beta, but the franchise’s full-fledged extraction mode is already running into hot debates. One of them involves the Possum trait, which lets operators come back from the dead once per match, with no time limit. The divisive perk has sparked a few discussions on Reddit and social media . Some use it as a means to avoid paying a hefty operator rescue fee, while others see it as particularly awful to go up against during team fights. Possum is one of two choices at the top of the Warfighter operator tree. If you have it equipped, you get one free life, even after your character is fully dead. There’s no time limit for Possum, either. You could take a 10-minute break and come back to life, ready to continue exploring Hajin again. Each player in a squad can also have it. Plus, any operator in DMZ can revive teammates after they’ve been gunned down. Image via Activision Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter ! With Possum, it’s possible to get back up and revive your squad with few penalties, outside of likely losing the gear you had on you. Naturally, though, the power to navigate life and death can lead to particularly disruptive scenarios , such as shifting the outcome of a fast-paced firefight. Unsurprisingly, seeing an opponent you just killed come back to get you can feel frustrating. In POIs, for instance, you could go back to looting after a skirmish, only to find a dead body suddenly disappeared. This is a common criticism from its detractors, while supporters think it makes the experience more forgiving, especially solo. Some of the traits in DMZ surely seem cranked up to 11. UAV Overwatch allowed players to gain infinite UAVs by activating them. There was no way to steal them back until a quick patch. Possum is bound to meet a similar fate. Despite being less than a week old, DMZ is also going through the age-old debate of PvE vs. PvP , which has become commonplace for extraction shooters. PvE isn’t necessarily off the table, Infinity Ward told Destructoid , though developers are happy with the mix they have at launch. Since DMZ is a live-service title, there’s room for tuning up traits like Possum and other potentially troublesome elements. it’s unlikely to be the last controversy surrounding the unforgiving game mode, however.
